html:
The Declaration of Independence of Ukraine was adopted by the Ukrainian parliament in Kyiv on 24 August 1991, days after the failed coup in Moscow. A referendum on 1 December 1991 confirmed it with about 90 percent voting yes.

Every region, including Crimea, had a majority for independence. Leonid Kravchuk was elected president the same day. A week later the leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus signed the Belovezha Accords, ending the Soviet Union. Ukraine inherited the third largest nuclear arsenal in the world and gave it up under the Budapest Memorandum of 1994 in return for promises to respect its borders. Russia broke those promises with the annexation of Crimea in 2014. 24 August is Independence Day in Ukraine.
